title: Japan’s New CIA Could Be Takaichi’s Trump Card
gist: Japan under PM Sanae Takaichi is building its first dedicated foreign HUMINT agency, a 'Japanese CIA' targeted for 2028, atop a new National Intelligence Council and a ~700-person National Intelligence Bureau created by May legislation. The author frames it as burden-sharing for Trump and a step toward Five Eyes integration, while warning that building real clandestine capability will take years.

insights.claim: Japan is undertaking its most substantial intelligence overhaul since 1945, aiming to create its own CIA-like foreign intelligence agency by 2028 to run clandestine HUMINT against China, North Korea and Russia.
insights.speaker: Derek Grossman
insights.so_what: Marks a structural shift in Japanese security posture and alliance burden-sharing.
insights.quote: Her government is undertaking the most substantial overhaul of Japan’s intelligence collection and analysis capabilities since 1945

insights.claim: May legislation created a cabinet-level National Intelligence Council chaired by the prime minister and a National Intelligence Bureau, already operational with roughly 700 staff, replacing the Cabinet Intelligence and Research Office, akin to the U.S. ODNI.

insights.so_what: Institutional foundation makes the 2028 goal credible.

insights.claim: Building an effective clandestine service will take years beyond establishment: Japan must recruit case officers, develop cover and settle legal questions on paying agents, false identities and nonofficial cover.

insights.claim: A Japanese CIA lets Tokyo show Washington it takes burden-sharing seriously, alongside April's loosening of arms-export restrictions to allow lethal weapons sales and revisions to its three core security documents.
